entities.summary: Bernhard Klemens Maria Hoffbauer Pius Grzimek was a German zoo director, zoologist, book author, editor, and animal conservationist in postwar West Germany. During the Third Reich, he served as a veterinarian in the army. After World War II, he popularized the study of animals and an interest in wildlife in Germany, becoming the public face of Frankfurt Zoo, producing a popular German magazine called Das Tier, giving radio talks and appearing on a popular television series Ein Platz für Tiere [A place for animals] in the 1950s and 60s, apart from producing a multi-volume encyclopedia on animals.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent zoo director and conservationist, Grzimek played a crucial role in popularizing wildlife studies and animal conservation in post-war Germany, inspiring a new generation of scientists and conservationists. His work contributed to the development of modern zoology and animal welfare policies.
